rounds.proof_sketch: When else branch is entered, idx+3 >= size. The extra iteration (i=4) computes elem_idx = idx+4 > size, so the guard 'elem_idx < size' is always false. With size=262144, threads entering else have idx>=262144, making all elem_idx values >=size. No operations execute in the else branch for this configuration.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation adds a 5th iteration (i=4) to a loop in the else branch. However, the else branch is only entered when idx+3 >= size, which mathematically guarantees idx+4 > size. The inner conditional 'if (elem_idx < size)' therefore always evaluates to false for the extra iteration. For the fixed input shape [16, 16384] with 262144 elements, the last thread taking the vectorized path handles elements 262140-262143, and all threads entering the else branch have idx >= 262144 with no valid elements to process. The mutation produces identical behavior for any input values.
rounds.kill_strategy: This mutant is unkillable under the fixed-shape contract. The mathematical relationship between the branch condition (idx+3 >= size) and the loop guard (elem_idx < size) makes the extra iteration unconditionally unreachable in effect.
rounds.recommendations: Mutation testing frameworks should include semantic equivalence detection that identifies when loop bound mutations are neutralized by inner conditionals. For this pattern, analyzing the relationship between outer branch predicates and inner guards could automatically classify such mutants as equivalent.
